_about: Settings for the Along the way page (engine/along/: build.py, router.js, page.html), at /melbourne/along/: pick two places, see a likely tram, train or bus route between them and what's a short walk from the stops you pass. Built from the Routes page's data (docs/melbourne/routes/data/) and the map's published layers. The engine names no city. Toronto's along.json explains the keys.
_unlisted: Live at its URL but kept out of the sitemap, the hub and the map (and marked noindex) until the user makes it public.
_skipModes: Modes left out of the routes: V/Line trains (mode rail) and coaches are regional services with their own fares and bookings, as Chicago's Metra (the user, November 19, 2026). Metro trains (mode subway), trams and buses stay.
_skipRoutes: The Night Network buses (941 to 982) run only on weekend nights, but Transport Victoria's feed gives them no night flag, so the Routes data has no family to drop them by (the user, November 19, 2026).
_express: Buses timed at the router's express speed: the Eastern Freeway SmartBuses (905 to 908, 440 to 570 m a minute end to end in the November 2026 weekday schedule) and 201 (383). The other SmartBuses (900 to 903) run at local speed (the user, November 19, 2026).
_attachStrip: Words dropped from both names when a described place is matched to a place an earlier layer lists.

_pois: As Toronto's. parks: the City of Melbourne's parks, then OpenStreetMap's park outlines across Greater Melbourne (the map's region_parks layer), 1.5 ha and up; a name in both is listed once. Unnamed outlines (OpenStreetMap's bare "Park" or "Reserve"), retarding basins, drainage, pipe and powerline reserves, freeway and railway strips, school grounds and a housing estate's lawns are left out; creek linear parks stay. No street layer: Melbourne's map has no business districts. The discovery layer (engine/discover/build.py) adds the City's public art and memorials (with the City's descriptions), the Victorian Heritage Register (history, each linked to its Heritage Database page) and viewpoints.

page.title: What’s along your commute?
page.description: Pick where you start and where you’re going in Melbourne and see a likely tram, train or bus route between them, two or three other ways to go, and what’s a short walk from every stop you pass: public art, heritage places, viewpoints, parks, landmarks, campuses, libraries and the names people use for parts of the city.
page.lede: You take the same tram, train and bus every day, past dozens of stops you’ve never got off at. Put in where you start and where you’re going to see what’s a short walk from each one, and a couple of other ways to make the trip.
page.credits: Routes and stops: Transport Victoria GTFS (CC BY 4.0) · Public art, memorials, the City’s parks and libraries, and the descriptions of artworks: City of Melbourne Open Data (CC BY 4.0) · Heritage places: Victorian Heritage Register, Heritage Council of Victoria via Vicmap (CC BY 4.0) · Viewpoints: Layers.City, from the Shrine of Remembrance’s and the City of Port Phillip’s pages · Parks across Greater Melbourne: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) · Landmarks and known-as names: Layers.City
page.outside: That spot is too far from a tram, train or bus stop. Try an address in Greater Melbourne.
page.noMatch: No match in Melbourne for “{q}”. Try the full street address, like “1 Spring St”.
page.noRoute: No route turned up between those two places. Try spots closer to a tram or bus stop or a station.
page.appButton: Take this trip in the app
page.caveat: A likely route, not directions: rides are timed at each mode’s usual speed and waits at half the usual gap between services. Check Transport Victoria or your maps app before you head out. What’s listed comes from this site’s own layers, the City of Melbourne’s data and the Victorian Heritage Register, so it’s far from everything that’s there.
page._tries: Placeholders until riders in Melbourne send three real commutes (the user, November 19, 2026).
